note: Includes successors after Dahir’s defeat in 712, following the source chronology.

note: Shows the Punjab phase from the Met chronology, ending with the last Lahore ruler. Earlier Afghanistan-based rule and raids are outside this bar.

name: Arghun
note: Uses the Met’s dynastic range, which includes a later period of reduced authority.

name: Gupta

name: Mughal
area: Northern subcontinent, later much of the Deccan
note: The gap marks Sur rule. Later emperors had greatly reduced power. The end follows the source’s formal abolition date of 1858, after the capture of Delhi in 1857.

name: Sharqi
note: Uses the Met range. Later claims beyond this period are not plotted.

note: A regional ruling house with increasing British dependence, ending in annexation.

name: Asaf Jahi
note: From 1724 the Nizams exercised substantial practical autonomy while acknowledging nominal Mughal suzerainty. French influence shaped the succession struggles of 1748–1762. The dotted phase begins with the permanent Company subsidiary alliance of 1798, strengthened in 1800. A solid bar means before British paramountcy, not complete formal independence.

name: British Raj · Crown rule

note: British Crown administration. Provinces under direct rule and princely states under paramountcy had different relationships with it. Annual dating includes the transfer year 1947.
